page.title: Best Ultralight Headlamp for Backpacking (2026): Weight, Lumens and Real Runtime
page.desc: The Nitecore NU25 MCT UL gives 400 lumens from 47 g, with USB-C and IP66. Real runtimes, owner complaints and the lighter, cheaper and AAA-powered alternatives.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best ultralight headlamp for backpacking is the Nitecore NU25 MCT UL ({buy:nitecore-nu25-mct-ul}): 400 lumens from 47 g (1.65 oz), USB-C charging in about 75 minutes, and IP66 sealing. Owners' top worry is battery life. High lasts only about 2 hours 40 minutes, but the lamp runs about 13 hours at 60 lumens and up to 45 hours at 6 lumens.

The lightest rechargeable headlamp here is the Petzl Bindi at 35 g. But it tops out at 200 lumens and still charges through an uncovered micro-USB port. The Nitecore NU20 Classic ({buy:nitecore-nu20-classic}) weighs 38 g and gives 360 lumens and USB-C. If you go many days between outlets and don't carry a power bank, the Black Diamond Spot 400 runs on AAA cells you can swap. Nitecore Store prices seen on 2026-11-10.

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • Short runtime on high (5 of the sources we read). Every light this small runs out quickly at full power. In an r/Ultralight sphere test, an earlier NU25 UL dropped from about 500 to about 175 lumens soon after turn-on, and held there. Treat 400 lumens as a burst for route-finding. The 60-lumen mode is the one you'll hike on.
  • Cord headbands (4). Testers say the NU25 UL's thin cords tangle, twist and get less comfortable over long hours. If that worries you, the NU25 MCT ({buy:nitecore-nu25-mct}) is the same lamp on a fabric band for 3 g more.
  • Fiddly controls (4). Owners mention two small buttons, many modes and no mode memory on the NU25 or the NU20. Learn the lockout before you pack the light.
  • Sealed batteries (3). None of the rechargeable lights here lets you swap the cell. Nitecore's warranty on lighting with a built-in battery is 24 months.
  • The Bindi's port (3). Testers and owners keep pointing to its open micro-USB port. It charges in about 4 hours and isn't sealed.

Which one by need

  • Thru-hiking and ultralight backpacking: NU25 MCT UL. It has the most light per gram, USB-C and IP66.
  • Lowest weight on a budget: NU20 Classic. It weighs 38 g and gives 360 lumens, plus a red light and a high-CRI reading light.
  • All-day comfort: NU25 MCT, with its wider fabric headband.
  • Absolute minimum weight, camp use only: Petzl Bindi, at 35 g and 200 lumens.
  • Long stretches with no charging: Black Diamond Spot 400. It takes 3 AAA cells and is rated IPX8.

Not recommended

Don't use a coin-cell clip light as your only headlamp. In the r/Ultralight test, the Black Diamond Flare gave 56 lumens on its included cells and was quite dim within 30 minutes. It works as a backup, not as a trail light.
